newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to down, LSFO loses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to down, LSFO loses.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to down slightly Wednesday in thin activity, with low sulphur still soft amid slack East Coast utility demand despite firmer gas prices, sources said.

"We may still see lower (low sulphur) numbers near-term, but city gate gas prices could put a floor under resid and demand should pick up soon," said one cash trader, noting prospects for better cooling loads as summer nears.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent fell slightly to $14.75-15.00 a barrel, with May one percent paper also losing some ground to $14.50-75, traders said.
Traders said recent gains in East Coast city gate gas prices should trigger some fuel switching to resid.
"Fuel is getting competitive with gas again. We may be out again (in the next week or so) for a spot (resid) piece," said one East Coast utility.
High sulphurs in New York held relatively steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged at $14.25-50, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was unchanged at $16.25.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent eased 10-15 cents to $14.75 or lower, while three percent held at $13.25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices jumped more than 15 cents Wednesday to about $2.50/mmBtu, or $15.75 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed 10 cents to about $2.20/mmBtu, or $13.86 a barrel.
